name: Georgia

notes: Groceries: exempt from the 4% state tax; local taxes apply to food sold to individuals for home consumption.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).
Gasoline: exempt from the 4% state tax; local sales taxes are prepaid by distributors on a price base capped at $3.00 a gallon.
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
gaps: Georgia cities levy no general sales tax of their own except Atlanta (and the consolidated city-county governments, whose rate is the county rate); every other city takes its county rate, so only places with their own rate are listed.

tiers.label: Georgia job tax credit tier
tiers.what: Sets the per-job state income tax credit (O.C.G.A. 48-7-40; Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-8-.36): $3,500 a year for each new job in Tier 1, $2,500 in Tier 2, $1,250 in Tier 3 and $750 in Tier 4, with the fewest new jobs required in Tier 1 and the most in Tier 4; the 40 least developed counties are Tier 1.
